family.note: Same shop/party-item domain and Func_08077008/Func_08015080/Value_XXXXXXXX-message idioms as the template, but a different owner entirely: this one draws a single item slot's detail panel (icon-id text, then one of three states -- a -4 result message, a -3 result message, or a quantity readout multiplied by (slot-flag>>11)+1) rather than the template's full multi-slot icon grid.

notes: Read the raw assembly directly: unit=Func_08077008(unit_id); slot_offset=item_id*2+216; masked=*(u16*)(unit+slot_offset)&0x1ff; mult=(*(u16*)(unit+slot_offset)>>11)+1 -- confirmed the reference genuinely re-loads the halfword with a second ldrh rather than reusing one cached value, which is why caching into a single `u16 value` local scored worse (wrong_instructions 50) than re-dereferencing at each use site (wrong_instructions 36, kept as the draft). If (window!=0): Func_08015270(window); Func_08015080(masked+(s32)&Value_00000182, window, 0, 0); result=Func_080772a8(unit_id,item_id); if(result==-4) draw Value_00000c94; else if(result==-3) draw Value_00000c95; else { qty=Func_080b19cc(*(u16*)(unit+slot_offset)); total=mult*qty; draw Value_00000c8d at (8,8), Func_080150b0(total,5,window,40,style=8), draw (Value_00000c8d-5) at (80,8) }.

The two message-id externs for the -4/-3 branches and the two related to the quantity line (Value_00000c94, Value_00000c95, Value_00000c8d) were assigned in pool-appearance order from the raw .4byte dump (0x1ff, 0x182, 0xc94, 0xc95, 0xc8d); their names are placeholders for 'the constant at that ROM address' per this project's Value_XXXXXXXX convention, not independently verified message text.

The former allocation/scheduling diagnosis was false. Although the source spelled two reads, GCC common-subexpression elimination merged them; the reference's two ldrh instructions prove that the original source treated those accesses as independently observable. Giving the two reads volatile semantics restores the reference's pseudo lifetimes and register allocation without compiler overrides or forced registers.
Exact under canonical flags: 212 candidate bytes, 212 reference bytes, 0 differing halfwords, and 0 wrong instructions. Adopted as Shop_DrawUseItemDetails.
